description.narrative: The project aims at scaling-up Multi-Hazard Early Warning System and the use of Climate Information in Georgia. GCF funded component.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative: 1.1/ a/ Procurement and installation of a telecommunication system; b/ Procurement and operationalization of HPC; c/ Observation equipment for 6 river basins (2 Automatic meteorological stations, 30 Automatic meteorological posts, 11 Automatic hydrological posts, 3 Snow Measurement equipment) d/ Procurement of 15 Agrometeorological Stations 1.2/ a/ Initiation of collection of LiDAR data b/ Initiation of development of hazard maps and risk profiles for 3 river basins: Supsa, Natanebi, Kintrishi. c/ Collection of hydro-meteorological and geological field data and processing of historical data for hazard-mapping for Enguri, Khobistskali and Mtkvari river basins (Mtkvari, within borders of Tbilisi). 1.3/ a/ Upgrading the GIS-based socio-economic model; b/ Socio-economic assessment for three river basins (Supsa, Natanebi, Kintrishi) completed. 1.4/ The conceptual design of the multi-hazard disaster risk information system (MHDRIS) developed. 2.1/ a/ Legal and Institutional frameworks for MHEWS and Capacity Assessment Report developed; b/ Capacity Development Plan developed and implemented c/ Awareness raising events in CCA/DRR conducted 2.2/ International technical advice delivered to NEA on: a/ Enhancing meteorological forecasting and satellite precipitation estimates; b/Providing service new source data/type into forecasting platform; c/Expanding flood forecasting platform (upgrading Rioni flood forecasting platform). 2.3/ Initiating preparatory activities. 3.1/ a/ Gender inputs provided on development of Capacity Assessment scorecard; b/ Gender inputs provided in documents regulating the legal and institutional frameworks for MHEWS and climate information issues c/ Gender inputs provided to implement Gender Action Plan (GAP) d/ Finalization of design of impact evaluation for non-structural measures 3.2/ No Targets 3.3/ a/ Project designs are developed for 2 structural measures and construction works initiated (LoA MRDI) b/ Additional surveys on Kobuleti site undertaken and construction initiated (LoA MRDI) 3.4/ a/ Training module on DRR/DRM, MHEWS, CBMHRM Developed b/ Education programs for youth developed (pre-school and university levels c/ Networking activities - community awards and community forum organized

1.1/ a, b, c/ tender for HPC, as well as tender for Observation equipment for 6 river basins (2 Automatic meteorological stations, 30 Automatic meteorological posts, 11 Automatic hydrological posts, 3 Snow Measurement equipment) has been announced. d/ Procurement of 15 Agrometeorological Stations and ICT system has been initiated 1.2/ a,b,c/ Development of hazard maps delayed. The project recruited a French company for the task, however, due to poor quality of the deliverables submitted and the failure of contract performance, the contract was terminated with the company. As a result, the project suffered significant delays in terms of development of the methodology for multi-hazard mapping and risk assessment, as well as completion of multi-hazard maps for 3 river basins. 1.3/ a, b/ In 2020 Unified Methodology of Gender-sensitive Socio-economic Vulnerability Assessment for multi-hazards and risks has been developed, however, due to the delays in development of hazard mapping the finalization is underway and thus methodology has not been presented with relevant stakeholders. 1.4/ In 2020 the conceptual design of the Multi Hazard Disaster Risk Information System has been developed. 2.1/ a, b, c/ The project started baseline capacity assessment, covering both institutional capacity assessment of each stakeholder, implemented by international and national experts in institutional capacity assessment and technical level capacity assessment to be supplemented by technical experts recruited within both projects. The team of experts developed initial capacity assessment report, based on the results further detailed assessment of institutional and technical capacities was initiated. 2.2/ a, b, c/ In 2020, Project started preparatory work related to the enhancement of meteorological forecasting, assessment of satellite precipitation estimates and acquisition and analysis of radar data for the inclusion into the forecasting platforms. A number of activities were also fulfilled for the achievement of operationalization of the Rioni River Flood Forecasting Platform. 2.3/Activity has not been started. 3.1/ a, b, c/ Interventions of CBEWS and CBCRM has not been started in 2020, due to the delays in development of risk maps. 3.2/ Baseline survey in the first 3 river basins of non-structural measures will be conducted in 2021. 3.3/ During 2020 preparatory works has been implemented such as a/ Preparation of Technical guidance document for the design of structural measures for the management for flood, landslide and other Risk Management structures at a national level b/ Initiation of review and update of the technical designs of structural measures for 5 sites as part of MRDI co-financing 3.4/ a, b, c/ Baseline numbers for the first 3 river basins in the areas of nun-structural measures will be defined in 2021

1.1 a/ 27 pieces of equipment is installed. b/ ICT is procured. Works are ongoing to operationalize the system. The contracted company is implementing the ICT system deployment c/ 15 pieces of geological equipment is procured d/ 15 pieced of geological equipment is delivered
1.2 a/ Multi-hazard maps for 3 river basins: Supsa, Natanebi, Kintrishi are developed. b/ ?/ Nationwide maps developed for drought, wind, hail, avalanche.
1.3 a/ Socio-economic vulnerability studies were conducted in 3 river basins. b/ Risk/receptor combinations have been worked out for Wind and Hailstorm nationwide, integrating their damage on property.
1.4 a/ System Requirements Specification (SRS) are identified; b/ System Design Specification are developed; c/ Final data sets and detailed hardware technical requirements specification are developed.
2.1 a/ Baseline Capacity Assessment Report for MHEWS is conducted. b/ Capacity Development Plan for MHEWS is developed. c/ Capacity Development Strategy for MHEWS was developed as an integral part of capacity development plan; d/ General institutional framework for MHEWS was developed; e/ Institutional framework for Risk Knowledge and Preparedness and Response Capabilities components under MHEWS checklist will be developed in 2023; f/ Consultations with the GoG on the implementation of the changes in the legal framework were initiated. Legal framework for Risk Knowledge and Preparedness and Response Capabilities components under MHEWS checklist will be finalized in 2023.
2.2 a/ Enhancing meteorological forecasting through introducing global model data (ECMWF outputs) to local model is ongoing; b/ Verification of quality of satellite and weather radar data for application in hazard forecasting platforms due to the absence of the expert. The activity will be renewed in 2023. c/ Verification of global model quality for application in hazard forecasting platforms is ongoing; d/ Hazard forecasting platforms is established. Data for 4 river basins are integrated into flood forecasting platform and is working in a testing mode.
2.3 a/ Development of strategy and action plan for integrating economic tools and approaches into the agricultural sector is ongoing to be finalized in 2023; b/ Framework for enhancement of advisory services developed. The draft of strategy and action plan on enhancement of advisory services in Georgia is developed to be finalized in 2023; c/ Two assessments of the needs and institutional capacities of State Agencies and other stakeholders were conducted.
2.4 a/Municipal preparedness and response plans were developed by EMS in selected 6 municipalities. b/ Preparatory works to develop basin-level multi-hazard risk management plans have launched and are in progress. ToR and RFP developed for preparation of MHRMP in 4 river basins in western Georgia.
3.1 a/ Gender issues were mainstreamed across all project activities. b/ Baseline assessment of Impact Evaluation/KAP survey for non-structural measures launched in the first 3 river basins; c/ The international expert set up a framework and processes for the implementation of CBDRM activities for the most vulnerable communities. 15 most vulnerable communities were identified within 3 river basins in west Georgia.
3.2 a/Awareness raising activities were conducted in 10 target municipalities directly covering 2022 people (with 68% of women). b/ Integration of DRR/DRM syllabuses in climate-change related faculties is in progress at one university. c/ 3 awards (school, media CBO awards), 1 community forum and 1 public-private-community dialogues was organized.
3.3 a/ Construction of three GCF-funded structural measures is ongoing. b/ Designs as well as constructions of five RD-financed sites were finalized. c/ GRM is in-place and is operational.

comment.narrative: MHEWS does not exist: institutional responsibilities and communication protocols for EWS, climate and disaster risk management are not properly defined. FFEWS is available only for the Rioni river basin.

Operational MHEWS for floods, landslides, mudflows, avalanches, hailstorms and droughts in place covering all major 11 river basins, including: multi-hazard forecasting platform, national warning communication protocols, telecommunication systems, warning dissemination systems. Warnings are tailored to the needs of vulnerable groups; Information on hazards delivered through multiple methods. Information is clear and not complex. Information is issued in understandable for the population languages.
